idea: uma app interna onde a equipa regista pedidos de férias e o gestor aprova ou recusa

areas.summary: Team members submit vacation requests and the manager approves or rejects them. Success: every vacation request goes through the app and the manager answers each within 2 business days; no more requests by email or word of mouth.
Up to 20 team members who submit requests a few times a year, and one single manager who reviews them as they arrive. Everyone uses email and a browser; nobody is technical.

v1: team members submit vacation requests (dates); the manager approves or rejects each. Out of scope: automatic tracking of remaining vacation days, payroll integration, other absence types (sick leave, absences).

One web form per request: start date, end date, optional comment (max ~500 chars); requester identity comes from login. Volume: a few requests per person per year, up to 20 people. Manager input: approve or reject per request, with an optional reason.

Requester gets an email with the decision (approved/rejected, plus reason if given) and sees each request's status (pending/approved/rejected) in the app. Manager sees a list of all pending requests in the app and gets an email when a new request arrives.

Google Workspace sign-in (OAuth with company Google accounts) for login; a transactional email service for notifications. If email sending fails: retry 3 times, then log the failure; the request status stays visible in the app. If Google sign-in is down, nobody can log in and the app shows a clear message; no data is lost.

Only company Google accounts can sign in. Team members can create and view only their own requests and cancel them while pending; only the manager can approve or reject; nobody can delete requests. Secrets (Google OAuth client secret, email service API key, database URL) live in .env / the host's environment variables, never in code. Test: if a team member who is not the manager tries to approve a request, the app refuses and the request stays pending.

TypeScript web app (Next.js) with a Postgres database, hosted on a managed service (Vercel + Supabase), reachable only by signing in with a company Google account. Why: always available to the whole team without maintaining a server. Test: if someone opens the app URL without signing in, they are sent to the Google sign-in page and see no request data.

areas.reason: Submitting and approving requests needs no judgement from a model; the manager decides.

areas.summary: Five failure cases: (1) end date before start date: form rejected with a clear message, nothing saved; (2) request overlapping one of the same person's pending or approved requests: rejected with a message; (3) email sending fails: retry 3 times, log the failure, status stays visible in the app; (4) manager clicks approve/reject twice or on an already decided request: the first decision stands, nothing changes; (5) sign-in with a non-company account: access refused, nothing shown. Test: if a request with end date before start date is submitted, it is rejected with a message and nothing is saved.

One Given/When/Then per requirement and per failure case, plus one happy-path end-to-end test: Given a team member signed in, When they submit a request and the manager approves it, Then the request shows Approved and the team member receives an approval email. Test: the end-to-end happy path above passes.

v1 is done when all acceptance tests pass, the app is deployed and reachable by the team with company Google accounts, a README explains how to run and deploy it, and one real request is submitted, approved and emailed by hand. Test: if the user submits one real request and the manager approves it in the deployed app, the requester receives the email and sees Approved.

history.question: Como vais saber que a app está a funcionar bem, sem abrir código?
history.recommended: Todos os pedidos de férias passam pela app e o gestor responde a cada um em 2 dias úteis; acabam os pedidos por email ou de boca.

history.question: Quantas pessoas tem a equipa, quantos gestores há, e com que à-vontade usam ferramentas digitais?
history.recommended: Uma equipa de até 20 pessoas com um único gestor; todos usam email e browser, nenhum é técnico.

history.question: O que é que a versão 1 não deve fazer, mesmo que pareça útil?
history.recommended: Sem contagem automática de dias de férias disponíveis, sem ligação ao processamento salarial e sem outros tipos de ausência (baixas, faltas).

history.question: Que informação é que a pessoa preenche ao fazer um pedido de férias?
history.recommended: Data de início, data de fim e um comentário opcional; o nome vem do login.

history.question: Como é que a pessoa fica a saber que o pedido foi aprovado ou recusado?
history.recommended: Recebe um email com a decisão e vê o estado do pedido na app; o gestor vê numa lista todos os pedidos pendentes.

history.question: Para enviar os emails e fazer login, a equipa já usa Google Workspace ou Microsoft 365?
history.recommended: Google Workspace: login com a conta Google da empresa e envio de emails por um serviço de email transacional; se o email falhar, tenta 3 vezes e o estado continua visível na app.

history.question: Onde deve a app ficar alojada para a equipa lhe aceder?
history.recommended: App web em TypeScript (Next.js) com base de dados Postgres, alojada num serviço gerido como Vercel com Supabase, acessível só a contas da empresa.
